context:
CopperQuay is a fictional freight broker reconciling shipper organizations across four booking systems. Identity means the legal contracting shipper, not a dock address or a route. There are 3.6 million records and many repeated warehouse addresses. The current nightly candidate generator unions exact scoped tax-ID matches with normalized-name-prefix plus country blocks. Common names create very large blocks. A developer reports a tenfold speedup after capping each block at 500 pairs and timing only successful worker tasks. The benchmark excluded retries, an output union stage, and deduplication of pairs emitted by both passes.

The nightly window is 45 minutes on a fixed worker pool; the actual full output volume and spill behavior are unknown. A past incident sample contains known missed matches, mostly from large customers. It is not a representative recall set. Mismerges are costly, but missing a shipper duplicate can also hide contract exposure. Engineers may run one isolated complete-output replay on a fixed snapshot and collect stage telemetry. No production configuration change is authorized.

Recommend a bounded cost and quality experiment. Compare physical execution changes preserving the required candidate set against at least one logical candidate-policy alternative. Specify comparison units, complete-output reconciliation, duplicate semantics, skew, retries and relevant retrieval recall evidence. Explain why a cap or a fast successful-task sample cannot by itself establish improvement. State which unknowns require a stop, what to measure within the available replay and what outcome would support or falsify the proposed next step.
title: CopperQuay candidate budget
